[PATH:empirical] Comparative case studies of regional innovation systems in Germany (e.g., automotive R&D in Baden-Württemberg) and Japan (e.g., electronics in Osaka) during periods of high-skilled immigration — Provides qualitative and quantitative evidence on whether wage premiums for native engineering PhDs rise when immigration occurs in saturated, narrow-tech R&D clusters versus diversified regions.

[PATH:theoretical] Agent-based or computational general equilibrium (CGE) model simulating labor market effects of high-skilled immigration under varying degrees of R&D sector concentration and innovation capacity saturation — Allows controlled testing of the causal mechanism: if the host region's innovation capacity is saturated, additional high-skilled immigrants may compete for limited complementary assets, raising native PhD wages due to increased demand for management and coordination skills in narrow tech fields.
